scenes.tts: Pasteur settled a real question: grape juice sealed from the air stayed inert, while juice open to airborne yeast foamed into alcohol.
scenes.narration: Pasteur settled a real question: grape juice sealed from the air stayed inert, while juice open to airborne yeast foamed into alcohol.

scenes.tts: Fermentation was biology: it appeared only alongside living, multiplying yeast. Pasteur invoked no vital force; his was an empirical claim, and a stronger one than his data required: that fermentation could not be separated from the living cell.
scenes.visual: yeast multiplies with fermentation; no vital force; data bar vs claim bar; cell holds fermentation

scenes.tts: From the very man who proved fermentation was alive, that conviction hardened into a forty-year orthodoxy, and it would take a flask of dead yeast to dissolve it.
scenes.visual: forty bricks of orthodoxy dissolved by a flask of dead yeast
